codeSnippets.output: Adds one <li> for the given note.

exercise.instruction: Complete the notes app. On load, read notes from localStorage key "notes" (default []). Build a render() function that clears #note-list and appends an li (created with createElement and appendChild) for each note. On form submit, preventDefault, trim the input, push the value to notes, save with localStorage.setItem + JSON.stringify, clear the input, and re-render. Call render() once on load.
hints: Hint 1: function render() { list.innerHTML = ""; notes.forEach((note) => { const li = document.createElement("li"); li.textContent = note; list.appendChild(li); }); }

Hint 2: form.addEventListener("submit", (event) => { event.preventDefault(); const value = input.value.trim(); if (!value) return; notes.push(value); input.value = ""; localStorage.setItem("notes", JSON.stringify(notes)); render(); });
Hint 3: render(); — call it once at the bottom to display any stored notes on load.

quiz.question: What does the || [] guard do when reading notes?
options: Defaults to an empty array when getItem returns null

quiz.question: When should you call save()?
options: Once at the end of the script
After every mutation of the notes array

quiz.question: Why does render() clear the list first?
options: To avoid duplicating items on every re-render
